title: Grade 2 Science — Thu, Jun 26
description: Animals and Their Young Ones — Day 4 of 5: Animals in groups vs alone; animal sounds
subject: science

questions.question: Which animal lives in a group called a 'herd'?
questions.explanation: Cows, elephants, deer and many plant-eating animals live in groups called herds. Tigers, eagles and snakes usually live alone.

questions.question: What sound does a dog make?
questions.explanation: Dogs bark. Cows moo, lions roar and sheep bleat.

questions.question: A group of fish swimming together is called a:
questions.explanation: A group of fish is called a school. A group of wolves is a pack, lions a pride and birds a flock.

questions.question: What sound does a cat make?
questions.explanation: Cats meow. Dogs bark, cows moo and lions roar.

questions.question: Which animal usually lives ALONE (not in a group)?
questions.explanation: Tigers are solitary animals — they live and hunt alone. Ants and bees live in large colonies; penguins live in large groups.

questions.question: What is a group of ants called?
questions.explanation: A group of ants is called a colony. Ant colonies can have millions of members working together.

questions.question: Match: 'A group of birds flying together' is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A group of birds is called a flock. When birds migrate, they fly in flocks for safety.

questions.question: Lions live in groups called 'prides'. The female lions (lionesses) do most of the hunting. This shows that:
options: Animals in groups sometimes share responsibilities
questions.explanation: In a lion pride, lionesses cooperate to hunt while the male lion protects the group. This shows animals in groups can divide roles and responsibilities.

questions.question: What sound does a frog make?
questions.explanation: Frogs croak. Dogs bark, snakes hiss and birds chirp.

questions.question: Why do some animals live in groups?
options: They are afraid of being alone
For safety, hunting together and caring for young ones
questions.explanation: Animals live in groups for many benefits: safety in numbers (harder to be attacked), cooperation in hunting and helping care for young ones.

questions.question: Which of these correctly matches animal and its sound?
questions.explanation: Snakes hiss. Cows moo, horses neigh and dogs bark. 'Dog-bleat' and 'Cow-bark' are wrong.

questions.question: Wolves hunt in 'packs'. Why is this an advantage?
options: They can hunt prey much larger than themselves by working together
questions.explanation: A single wolf cannot easily hunt a large deer, but a pack can surround and exhaust the prey. Group hunting allows wolves to catch prey they could not catch alone.

questions.question: Bees live in colonies with a queen, workers and drones. Each has a different job. What does this tell us?
options: Bees are confused about their roles
Bee colonies have a complex social structure with division of labour
All bees do the same work
questions.explanation: Bee colonies show division of labour — the queen lays eggs, workers collect food and protect the hive, and drones mate with the queen. This organised system makes the colony highly efficient.

questions.question: Animal sounds serve as communication. A mother hen clucks in a special way when danger is near. What does this show?
options: Animal sounds can warn others of danger — a form of communication
questions.explanation: Mother hens have different clucks for different situations — a warning call brings chicks to hide. This shows that animal sounds are a form of communication, not just random noise.

questions.question: Migratory birds travel in flocks of thousands. Arrange these benefits of group migration in order of importance (most to least):
options: Safety + navigation help + energy saving (flying in V-formation)
questions.explanation: Flying in flocks offers multiple benefits: safety (harder for predators), navigation (experienced birds lead), and energy saving (V-formation reduces wind resistance). All three benefits matter.
